title: Account Executive
mission: Turn qualified meetings into signed customers by running a clear, honest sales process.
outcomes_90_days: Run own pipeline in the CRM with every deal having a next step and a date.
Reach a first closed deal and a repeatable win rate the team tracks monthly.
Send proposals within a day of the final call, using the company template.
Give product and pricing feedback from lost deals every month.

criteria.name: Discovery and qualification
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Asks questions that reveal the problem, who decides, budget and timing, and says no to poor fits early.
evidence_needed: Describes questions asked and what they learned
Example of a deal they walked away from and why
Names who decided and how they found out
levels: 0 no evidence of discovery and qualification
1 names discovery and qualification but gives no example
2 discovery and qualification done with guidance or at small scale
3 discovery and qualification done independently with a clear result
4 discovery and qualification with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows discovery and qualification with real examples

criteria.name: Track record of closing
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Has closed deals of a similar size and cycle and can explain the steps from first call to signature.
evidence_needed: Deal sizes and cycle lengths with real numbers
Win rate or quota attainment, with how it was measured
One deal story with the hardest moment

gates.question: Can the person legally work in the country of the role?

deal_breakers.description: Describes promising features or results the company cannot deliver in order to close.
deal_breakers.job_related_reason: Overpromising leads to refunds, churn and legal risk.

work_sample.title: Discovery call plan and follow up
work_sample.brief: You get a fictional lead's notes and a one page price list. Write your 10 discovery questions in order, then a follow up email after the call and a short proposal outline (scope, price, next step). State what you would need to know before sending the proposal.
work_sample.how_to_score: Score question quality (problem, decision process, budget, timing), honest scope, clear next step, no invented product claims, and whether risks and unknowns are named.

interview_questions.question: Tell me about a deal you chose not to pursue. How did you know?
good_answer_signs: Names a clear signal such as no budget or no decision maker
Saved time for a better deal

interview_questions.question: Take me through your last closed deal from first call to signature. What almost went wrong?
good_answer_signs: Gives dates, amounts and people involved by role
Names a real obstacle and what they did

interview_questions.question: How do you decide which deals to work on today and which to drop from your forecast?
good_answer_signs: Uses stage, next step date and last contact
Removes stale deals on a schedule

red_flags: Quotes revenue numbers with no way to check them
Speaks badly about every past customer
Cannot say what the product does not do
Discounts first and asks questions later
sourcing_channels: Referrals from your own customers and partners
Industry associations and local business groups
Former colleagues of your best salespeople
pay_research_hint: Compare the base and the commission plan: look at several current postings and a published pay survey for the region. Ask what share of reps hit quota in comparable companies if you can find that.
automation_note: AI can prepare call notes, draft proposals and keep the CRM tidy. The relationship, judgment on price and the final yes stay with a person.
